QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_49

question.text: Under the default waterfall mechanism of the Clearing Corporation, what is the correct sequence for utilising resources to cover a member's default?

answer.text: Monies of the defaulting member → Insurance (if any) → CC resources equal to 5% of segment MRC → Core SGF of the segment (penalties, CC contribution and remaining Core SGF pro-rata) → Remaining CC resources → Approved CC/SE resources from other segments → Capped additional contribution by non-defaulting members → Pro-rata payout haircut
Core SGF first → Defaulter's margin → CC's resources → Insurance → Other members' contributions
CC's own resources first → Core SGF → Defaulter's margin → Insurance → Other members' contributions
Insurance proceeds first → Defaulter's margin → Core SGF → CC's resources → Other members' contributions

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook waterfall is: (1) monies of the defaulting member (margins, deposits, other assets with the CC), (2) insurance, if any, (3) CC resources equal to 5% of the segment MRC, (4) Core SGF of the segment — applied as penalties first, then the CC's contribution, then the remaining Core SGF pro-rata, (5) remaining CC resources, (6) approved CC/SE resources from other segments, (7) capped additional contribution from non-defaulting members and finally (8) a pro-rata payout haircut. The Trap: Core SGF does NOT come before insurance and the CC's own skin-in-the-game (5% of segment MRC). The CC's first tranche of own resources is applied before the Core SGF is broken into, and insurance (where available) is used before either. Note: The Core SGF itself has an internal order: penalties collected from members, then the CC's own contribution, then the remaining Core SGF balance pro-rata. This sub-order keeps the CC's incentives aligned with prudent risk management.
